story_title: The Evolution of Natural Disaster Mortality: A Century of Data Insights
story_subtitle: Analyzing the deadliest natural disasters, their trends, and human impact across the 20th century

story_pieces.narration: Total natural disaster deaths peaked in 1917 with 2.5 million fatalities, driven by epidemics, while the lowest recorded deaths were in 2017 with just 499 deaths. This stark contrast highlights major shifts in disaster resilience and mortality patterns.
story_pieces.question: When did the deadliest year for natural disasters occur, and how has mortality changed over the century?
story_pieces.visualization: line chart (years vs. total deaths with trend line)

story_pieces.narration: Droughts caused 3 million deaths in 1928 and 1921, surpassing other disaster types. Earthquakes, particularly in 1976, caused over 276,000 deaths, while epidemics in 1917 and 1909 accounted for over 2.5 million and 1.5 million deaths respectively.
story_pieces.question: Which natural disaster type caused the most deaths, and were there any singular events with outsized impacts?
story_pieces.visualization: bar chart (disaster types vs. top annual deaths with highlights)

story_pieces.narration: Extreme weather events saw a dramatic rise in deaths from 1970 (304,495) to 1973 (434,400), reflecting heightened vulnerability or improved reporting. Conversely, flood deaths in 1931 reached 3.7 million, the highest recorded for this category.
story_pieces.question: How have extreme weather deaths evolved over time, and were there any exceptional spikes?
story_pieces.visualization: area chart (years vs. extreme weather deaths with anomaly markers)

story_pieces.narration: Epidemics accounted for 63% of all disaster-related deaths between 1900-1920, but their share dropped to 17% by 2010. This shift suggests changing patterns in disaster types and public health advancements.
story_pieces.question: How has the proportion of deaths from different disaster types changed over the century?
story_pieces.visualization: donut chart (time periods vs. proportion of deaths by disaster type)

story_pieces.narration: Between 1900-1940, drought deaths averaged 280,000 annually, whereas from 1960-2017, the average dropped to 148,000. This decline may indicate improved drought management strategies or better data collection.
story_pieces.question: Has the mortality impact of droughts decreased over time, and what factors might explain this trend?
story_pieces.visualization: grouped bar chart (decades vs. average drought deaths)
